documents.unit: Office of Student Conduct (Dean of Students Office)
documents.title: Know the Code Resources: Faculty and Staff (Artificial Intelligence section)
documents.stance_why: The document sets no AI rule of its own: AI tools "may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations", and faculty are only "encouraged to clearly communicate expectations". The decision is handed to instructors, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: The Office of Student Conduct's faculty page has a short AI section that treats generative AI as permitted, restricted or prohibited depending on the course, assignment or instructor. It urges instructors to state expectations in syllabi, points to CELT syllabus language and sample AI statements, and advises against relying on AI detectors alone.

units.why: The sentence says AI tools "may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations", so the university sets no single rule and leaves it to course, assignment or instructor. P04 fits better than P05 because no named tiers are defined.
units.anchor: may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations.

units.why: "faculty and instructors are encouraged to clearly communicate expectations regarding AI use in their syllabi, assignment instructions, and course discussions" asks instructors to state AI expectations; "encouraged" makes it a should, addressed to instructors at course start. P09 is the type for stating AI expectations in syllabus or assignments.
units.anchor: faculty and instructors are encouraged to clearly communicate expectations regarding AI use in their syllabi

units.why: "The use of AI is not inherently academic misconduct" tells faculty that AI use alone is not a violation, framing when AI use becomes a conduct issue. P36 is the nearest type (classification of AI use as misconduct); modality is informs because it states a boundary rather than an order.
units.anchor: The use of AI is not inherently academic misconduct.

units.why: "concerns arise when AI is used in a manner that violates course expectations, provides unauthorized assistance, or replaces the student's own demonstration of learning" defines which AI uses count as conduct concerns, i.e. classification of improper AI use as an integrity matter (P36); it is a definition so modality is informs.
units.anchor: concerns arise when AI is used in a manner that violates course expectations
units.policy: Concerns arise when AI is used in a manner that violates course expectations, provides unauthorized assistance, or replaces the student's own demonstration of learning.

units.why: "faculty should focus on course expectations ... rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone" tells instructors not to treat AI detectors as sufficient evidence; "should" and the detector reference make it P39 rather than P40, since it limits reliance rather than endorsing tools.
units.anchor: rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone
units.policy: When evaluating concerns, faculty should focus on course expectations, assignment requirements, the student's work product, and any other relevant information rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone.

units.why: "CELT has developed resources that may assist faculty in developing syllabus language, discussing AI use with students, and designing assignments" describes teaching-center support for faculty on AI policy and assignment design, matching P63 (resources for faculty); informs since it describes resources.
units.anchor: CELT has developed resources that may assist faculty in developing
units.policy: CELT has developed resources that may assist faculty in developing syllabus language, discussing AI use with students, and designing assignments and assessments that align with course learning objectives.

units.why: "Faculty may also review the Office of Student Conduct's guidance regarding referrals involving suspected unauthorized AI use" points faculty to referral guidance for suspected unauthorized AI use; it concerns handling suspected misuse (P36) and is a "may" pointer, not a rule.
units.anchor: guidance regarding referrals involving suspected unauthorized AI use
units.policy: Faculty may review the Office of Student Conduct's guidance regarding referrals involving suspected unauthorized AI use.

units.why: "Clearly communicate course and assignment expectations regarding AI use, including whether use is permitted, restricted, or prohibited" is a recommended strategy to state AI expectations; P09 fits and the "consider the following strategies" frame makes it should.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate course and assignment expectations regarding AI use, including whether use is permitted

units.why: "Discuss appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI within the context of your discipline and course learning objectives" asks instructors to talk with students about proper AI use. It is not a syllabus statement (P09), a tier (P05) or ask-first advice (P10); no type covers in-class discussion of acceptable AI use, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Discuss appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI within the context of your discipline
units.uncovered_note: Instructors discuss appropriate and inappropriate AI uses with students in class, in the context of the discipline (a communication practice other than a syllabus statement).

units.why: "Design assignments that require students to demonstrate their own learning, reasoning, analysis, and application of course concepts" recommends redesigning assignments in response to AI; P35 fits, and it is a should for instructors before the course.
units.anchor: Design assignments that require students to demonstrate their own learning, reasoning, analysis, and application

units.why: "Consider incorporating drafts, reflections, process documentation, in-class work, presentations" proposes assessment formats that show how students reached their product; P35 fits better than P26 because it is a design option for instructors, not a student submission duty.
units.anchor: Consider incorporating drafts, reflections, process documentation, in-class work, presentations

units.why: "Encourage students to seek clarification when they are unsure whether a particular use of AI or another resource is permitted" is the ask-before-using rule (P10), addressed to instructors who should encourage it.
units.anchor: Encourage students to seek clarification when they are unsure whether a particular use of AI

units.why: "consider discussing the student's work and process with them as part of gathering relevant information" tells instructors to talk with the student when concerns arise, before concluding misuse, which is P57.
units.anchor: consider discussing the student's work and process with them as part of gathering relevant information

units.why: "Online study, tutoring, answer-sharing, and AI platforms may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations and instructor authorization" says AI platform use depends on course expectations and instructor authorization, so P04.
units.anchor: may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations and instructor authorization
units.policy: Online study, tutoring, answer-sharing, and AI platforms may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations and instructor authorization.

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to communicate clear expectations regarding the use of these resources in their syllabi, assignments, and course discussions" repeats the communication request for study sites and AI tools in a separate section; a should for instructors, type P09.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to communicate clear expectations regarding the use of these resources

units.why: "CELT and the Office of Student Conduct have created ... sample statements regarding the use of artificial intelligence" offers ready-made AI syllabus statements to faculty; it is support for instructors writing policy (P63), not a tier definition (P05) since no tiers are listed in the text.
units.anchor: sample statements regarding the use of artificial intelligence
units.frag_end: regarding the use of artificial intelligence
units.policy: CELT and the Office of Student Conduct have created sample statements regarding the use of artificial intelligence.

units.why: The tutorial discussion question "What should a student do when they are unsure whether a resource, an AI tool, or a form of collaboration is allowed?" prompts class discussion of asking when unsure about AI use, so P10; it is a "may" suggestion for instructors.
units.anchor: unsure whether a resource, an AI tool, or a form of collaboration is allowed?

notes: Only one included document (Office of Student Conduct faculty page); only its AI section and AI-related sentences were coded. General academic-misconduct text without an AI reference was not coded. The collect notes say the CELT syllabus-options page was not resolved.
